column3: “At the beginning” is rendered “previously.”
“Susa the citadel” is rendered “the citadel of Susa,” and “the canal of Ulai” “the Ulai Canal.”
“High” is rendered “long,” and “one ram” “a ram.”
“Thrusting” is rendered “butting,” and “hand” “power”; NASB adds “other.”
“The he-goat of the goats” is rendered “a male goat,” and “a horn of conspicuousness” “a conspicuous horn.”
“In the rage of his strength” is rendered “in his mighty wrath.”
“Broke” is rendered “shattered,” and “hand” “power.”
“Up to muchness” is rendered “exceedingly”; NASB supplies “horns” with “four conspicuous.”
“From a small thing” is rendered “a rather small horn”; NASB supplies “Land” with “the Beautiful.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Perpetual” is rendered “regular sacrifice,” and “Commander” is capitalized; NASB adds “to be equal with.”

The Hebrew is difficult; “an army will be set over the perpetual in transgression” is rendered “on account of transgression the host will be given over to the horn along with the regular sacrifice,” supplying “the horn.” The meaning is uncertain.
“The perpetual” is rendered “the regular sacrifice,” and “desolate” “causes horror”; NASB supplies “apply” and “so as to allow.”
“Evening morning” is rendered “evenings and mornings”; “put right” is rendered “properly restored,” and “sanctuary” “holy place.”
“I sought understanding” is rendered “I sought to understand it”; “like the appearance of a man” is rendered “one who looked like a man.”
“Between Ulai” is rendered “between the banks of Ulai.”
“Was terrified” is rendered “was frightened,” and “son of humankind” “Son of man.”
“I was dazed” is rendered “I sank into a deep sleep”; NASB adds “upright.”
“The end of the indignation” is rendered “the final period of the indignation.”
NASB adds “represents.”
“The hairy he-goat” is rendered “the shaggy goat”; “the king of Greece” is rendered “the kingdom of Greece,” and NASB adds “represents.”
NASB supplies “horn” and “represent,” and renders “from a nation” as “from his nation.”
“Strong of face” is rendered “Insolent,” and “understanding of intrigues” “skilled in intrigue.”
“Wonders he will destroy” is rendered “he will destroy to an extraordinary degree”; “a people of holy ones” is rendered “the holy people.”
“By his hand” is rendered “by his influence,” “in prosperity” “while they are at ease,” “stand on” “oppose,” and “by not a hand” “without human agency.”
NASB adds “in the future.”
“I was done in” is rendered “exhausted”; NASB adds “again.”
